## Description

["Private escape sequences"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code#Fp_Escape_sequences) are escape sequences that are reserved for private use, though `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are commonly used for storing and restoring the current cursor position. When those escape codes are not stripped the cursor jumps around and causes Rich to write garbage output. An example of a program that uses this cursor store/restore functionality is the APK package manager in Alpine Linux:

https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/apk-tools/-/blob/48d91f482eb48a0a107b714ee183bb7e07782e14/src/print.c#L232-240

This commit updates the ANSI parser to ignore the `\x1b0`-`\x1b?` escape sequences, thus preventing them from being printed and causing havoc.

steps.message:
The issue is that "private escape sequences" (ANSI escape codes in the range `\x1b0` through `\x1b?`) are not being stripped by the ANSI parser in `rich/ansi.py`. This causes cursors to jump around and results in garbage output when processing output from certain programs (like `apk` in Alpine Linux).

The current regular expression `re_ansi` in `rich/ansi.py` matches:
1. OSC (Operating System Command) sequences: `\x1b\](.*?)\x1b\\`
2. CSI (Control Sequence Introducer) sequences and other escape sequences: `\x1b([(@-Z\\\_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~])`

The second part `[(@-Z\\\_]` matches characters from `@` (ASCII 64) to `Z` (ASCII 90) and some others. However, it does not match characters from `\x00` (null) to `?` (ASCII 63). To strip private escape sequences `\x1b0` through `\x1b?`, we need to expand this character range.

The range `\x1b0` to `\x1b?` corresponds to ASCII characters 48 ('0') to 63 ('?'). 
The current range `[@-Z\\\_]` starts at `@` (64). 
Expanding this to `[0-Z\\\_]` would include `0` (48) through `Z` (90).

FILES: rich/ansi.py:12
ROOT CAUSE: The `re_ansi` regex doesn't include the range `\x00` to `?` (ASCII 0-63) for single-character escape sequences following `\x1b`, allowing private escape sequences to pass through.
CHANGE: Update the regex `r\"(?:\\x1b\](.*?)\\x1b\\)|(?:\\x1b([(@-Z\\\_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))\"` to `r\"(?:\\x1b\](.*?)\\x1b\\)|(?:\\x1b([0-Z\\\_]|\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]))\"` (or similar to cover `0-?`). Actually, the issue says `\x1b0` to `\x1b?`, which is exactly what's missing before `@`. So replacing `[@-Z\\\_]` with `[0-Z\\\_]` should cover it, though technically `0-9` and `:;<=>?` are the specific targets.

TEST: tests/test_ansi.py (New test cases should be added to verify that sequences like `\x1b7` and `\x1b8` are stripped).
